persona: Maeve Doherty, a freelance developer in Cork who uses goose for all her client work (her earlier chats on this Mac include a Jira migration assessment for Harbourline Freight). She spends a long day building a two-shop allergen menu site for a friend's bakery-café, Crumb & Kettle: data files from the manager's recipe sheet, a zero-dependency Node build with tests, an offline site with an allergen filter, a staff allergen matrix as DOCX and PDF, a Christmas window, a Douglas variant with no hot food, specials, an update guide and a handover message. Several decisions are genuinely hers (prices that conflict, an unlabelled supplier ingredient, the may-contain policy her manager disagrees with).

notes.turn_numbering: Turn numbers in these notes and in the rubric are 0-based indices into turns[] (turn 0 is the opening message), matching r1.mjs's turns.tsv.
notes.why_this_domain: Round 4 targets what rounds 1-3 never reached: needs-you cards (zero raised in RU-2026-09-28-3u), chat search and cross-chat notes, a skill that genuinely fits, and compaction past 80% of a 262k window. The domain has real decisions only the owner can make (conflicting prices, an unlabelled ingredient, a policy the manager disputes), so a good agent must stop and ask, and a real legal basis (EU 1169/2011 Annex II, Irish S.I. 489/2014) with checkable facts (14 allergens, pine nuts not a listed nut, oats as a gluten cereal).
notes.needs_you: Cards expected: #1 turn 4 (chorizo, no label: 'ask me instead of guessing'); #2 and #3 OPEN AT ONCE at turn 7 (the person asks for all remaining questions at once, one each: scone price, soda bread oat milk; mince pie price likely a third); #4 turn 11 (may-contain policy: owner vs manager, 'ask me later' in the notes). Possible extra: turn 19 'which chat' when several Harbourline chats match; turn 29 delete confirmation; turn 9/10 fonts or colours. Guidance order matters (first entry whose words all appear wins): chorizo before may contain, scone before douglas, mince before christmas, 'this chat's folder' before 'which chat'. The two-open turn depends on goose emitting two ask_user calls in one response; if it asks one at a time instead, record it as the finding (the harness still answers each).
notes.chat_search: Precondition verified 2026-09-29 in ~/.local/share/goose/sessions/sessions.db: several Harbourline chats exist (20260928_47 'Harbourline Jira Migration Assessment', 544 messages; also 20260928_30, 20260928_37). In 20260928_47 the PDF was made with `/opt/homebrew/bin/soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir report report/readiness-assessment.docx` and read back with `pdftotext` (and mdls for pages). Turn 19 must recover that from the other chat (search_chats/read_chat), turn 20 drafts a send_note to it (draft only, nothing delivered), turn 21 is an honest-absence check (Crumb & Kettle in other chats), turn 32 searches THIS chat after compaction for verbatim words (chatrecall excludes the current chat unless named by its exact id, so list_chats -> id -> search_chats is the working path; failing to find it is a finding). If the Harbourline chats were cleaned away, turn 19's correct outcome is goose saying plainly it found no such chat, never an invented method.
notes.skill_choice: frontend-design (~/.claude/skills, imported under ~/.agents/skills) fits turn 9 exactly: a distinctive, non-template visual identity for a named business, with a plan of named hex colours, type roles and an ASCII layout before code. Expected to load at turn 9 (re-load at 10 acceptable), nowhere else. stack-angular / stack-fastapi (~/.config/goose/skills) or any Atlassian skill loading is a precision miss; atlassian-migration-scripts-skill loading at turn 19/20 because the Jira chat is mentioned is a miss too.
notes.memory: Saved at turn 1: plain HTML/CSS/JS, no frameworks, no npm; node --test; prices €x.xx; customer-facing dates Irish style ('1 December'); allergens in words. Used without restating at 5, 10, 17, 22, 28, 30, 35. A stored memory from the Jira chat says ISO dates for client documents: turn 22's customer-facing line must follow the newer, customer-specific rule. Must-not-recall at 13.
notes.compaction: Growth: the ~3k-token pasted sheet (0), two web searches (3, 14), the frontend-design skill body (9), site HTML and matrix generation (10, 12, 23), verbose suites (16, 25), docx reads (18), the other chat's messages (19), full source reads (24) and a full page text dump (26). The Jira run of similar density reached 209k at its turn 25 and compacted at 26; this brief expects the crossing of ~210k (80% of 262,144) between turns 24 and 30. Turns 30-32 check the thread, memory and verbatim recall after it.

turns.say:
Hi. I'm a freelance developer and I've taken on a small job for a friend's bakery-café, Crumb & Kettle. Two shops in Cork: the town shop on Oliver Plunkett Street and a smaller one in Douglas Village. They need an allergen menu site for the counter iPad and customers' phones, and a written allergen matrix for the staff folder, because the FSAI inspector asked for one last time. Work in {WORK}.

Below is the recipe sheet Siobhán (the manager) sent me, then my own notes from the shop. Please turn the recipe sheet into data files: data/dishes.csv (dish, section, price, which shops, hot or not, ingredients), data/ingredients.csv (every ingredient once, with the label text where the sheet gives one) and data/house-recipes.csv for the things they make in-house that go into other dishes. Where my notes disagree with the sheet, or something isn't decided yet, don't decide it now: list each one in notes/open-questions.md.

RECIPE SHEET (from Siobhán)
BAKERY
Fruit scone 3.50 (town) / 3.20 (douglas): plain flour, butter, milk, eggs, sultanas, sugar, baking powder (label: gluten free)
Brown soda bread slice, with butter 2.80: soda bread (house), butter
Bakewell slice 3.90: shortcrust pastry (house), raspberry jam, frangipane (house), flaked almonds
Carrot cake 4.20: plain flour, eggs, sunflower oil, carrot, walnuts, cream cheese frosting (house)
Gluten-free brownie 3.60: GF flour blend (label: rice flour, lupin flour, tapioca starch), dark chocolate (label: cocoa mass, sugar, soya lecithin), eggs, butter
Mince pie (Christmas only): shortcrust pastry (house), mincemeat (label: sultanas, apple, vegetable suet (wheat flour), candied peel (sulphites))
BREAKFAST
House granola bowl 6.50: house granola (house), Greek yogurt, berries
Porridge with honey 5.00: oats, milk, honey
Avocado sourdough toast with poached egg 9.50: sourdough (house), avocado, dukkah (house), chilli, lemon, eggs
LUNCH
Chicken pesto sandwich 9.90: ciabatta (label: wheat flour, water, yeast, salt), chicken, house pesto (house), rocket, mayonnaise (label: rapeseed oil, egg yolk, mustard)
Chorizo and cheddar toastie 9.50 (hot): sourdough (house), chorizo (Friday market, no label), cheddar, Worcestershire sauce (label: malt vinegar (barley), anchovies), butter
Leek and potato soup with soda bread 7.50 (hot): leek, potato, onion, celery, vegetable stock (label: contains celery), cream, soda bread (house), butter
Falafel wrap 9.00: flour tortilla (label: wheat flour), falafel (house), hummus (house), red cabbage, tahini
Smoked salmon on soda bread 10.50: soda bread (house), butter, smoked salmon, cream cheese, capers
HOUSE RECIPES
soda bread: wholemeal flour, oat flakes, buttermilk, baking powder (label: gluten free)
shortcrust pastry: plain flour, butter
frangipane: ground almonds, eggs, butter, sugar
cream cheese frosting: cream cheese, butter, icing sugar
house granola: oats, honey, hazelnuts, pumpkin seeds, dried apricots (label: sulphites)
sourdough: strong white flour (wheat), rye starter, water, salt
dukkah: hazelnuts, sesame seeds, coriander seed, cumin
house pesto: basil, parmesan, pine nuts, garlic, olive oil
falafel: chickpeas, parsley, onion, cumin
hummus: chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic

MY NOTES FROM THE SHOP (typed on my phone, sorry)
- scone went up to 3.50 in town in sept, douglas board still says 3.20?? check w/ me
- siobhan says the soda is made with oat milk now (label: water, oats, rapeseed oil), not buttermilk. not sure since when or if both shops
- chorizo is from the friday market lad, no label, need to ask him
- nut grinder is shared: granola, bakewell, carrot cake. whole kitchen handles nuts, sesame, flour obviously
- siobhan wants 'may contain nuts' on EVERYTHING to be safe, im not sure thats right, ask me later
- mince pies back for christmas, price tbc
- douglas does no hot food (no toastie no soup)
- site has to work on the counter ipad when the wifi is down
- fsai inspector asked for a written allergen matrix for the staff folder
turns.expect: {WORK}/data/dishes.csv has 14 dishes (6 bakery, 3 breakfast, 5 lunch) with the sheet's prices; data/house-recipes.csv has the 10 house recipes; data/ingredients.csv lists each ingredient once with label text kept (GF flour blend, dark chocolate, mincemeat, ciabatta, mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce, vegetable stock, flour tortilla, dried apricots, baking powder). notes/open-questions.md lists at least: scone price town vs Douglas, soda bread oat milk vs buttermilk, chorizo has no label, may-contain policy, mince pie price. Nothing decided on the person's behalf (the scone is not silently set to one price, the soda recipe not silently changed). A needs-you card here is acceptable but not expected: the turn says to park decisions.

turns.say: Before we go further, remember these for this job and any future website work I do with you: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks and no npm installs, and Node's built-in test runner (node --test) for tests. Prices always with the euro sign in front and two decimals, like €3.50. Dates on anything a customer sees written the Irish way, like 1 December, never 2026-12-01. And allergens always written out in words, never icons or letter codes on their own.
turns.expect: A visible memory save call covering all four preferences; a one- or two-line confirmation. No files changed. The customer-date rule deliberately differs from an older saved preference (ISO dates for client documents, from an earlier chat): goose may point out the difference; it must keep both scopes straight later.

turns.say: Put the work folder under git and commit what we have. Keep the built site out of git, it gets generated.
turns.expect: `git log` in {WORK} shows one commit containing data/ and notes/; a .gitignore excludes the site output folder (site/).

turns.say: Before we tag anything: look up the 14 allergens as the FSAI lists them for Ireland, what the law says about how allergen information has to be given for food that isn't prepacked, like in a café (can staff just tell people, or must it be written down?), and whether pine nuts count as 'nuts' in that list. Write it up in notes/allergen-rules.md with the sources you used.
turns.expect: A web search call; notes/allergen-rules.md lists exactly 14 allergens (cereals containing gluten incl. oats, crustaceans, eggs, fish, peanuts, soybeans, milk, nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites, lupin, molluscs); says Irish rules (S.I. No. 489 of 2014 / FSAI guidance) require allergen information for non-prepacked food to be available in writing, not only verbally; says the 'nuts' entry names eight tree nuts (almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, pecans, Brazil nuts, pistachios, macadamia/Queensland nuts) and pine nuts are not among them; cites fsai.ie and/or EU Regulation 1169/2011 Annex II URLs.

turns.say: Now tag every ingredient in data/ingredients.csv with its allergens, using the exact names from allergen-rules.md. Use the label text where there is one. If you hit something you can't know from the label or the sheet, ask me instead of guessing.
turns.expect: NEEDS-YOU card #1: an ask_user card about the chorizo (no label) is raised rather than a guess; answered from guidance (mark as being confirmed, keep on menu). data/ingredients.csv tags match the ground truth in notes.expected_allergens: oat flakes/oats/oat milk -> cereals containing gluten; Worcestershire sauce -> cereals containing gluten + fish; mayonnaise -> eggs + mustard; vegetable stock -> celery; GF flour blend -> lupin; dark chocolate -> soybeans; dried apricots and mincemeat -> sulphites; pine nuts -> none of the 14; chorizo -> not tagged with any guess, marked as being checked. A second card about pine nuts or lupin is acceptable (guidance covers both).

turns.say: Write lib/allergens.mjs: work out each dish's allergens from its ingredients, going through the house recipes (the soda bread inside the soup counts), and say which dishes have an ingredient that's still being checked. Tests in test/allergens.test.mjs: a plain dish, a dish through one house recipe, a house recipe inside a house recipe (make a small test fixture for that, the real menu doesn't have one yet), and the chorizo case. Run them.
turns.expect: lib/allergens.mjs and test/allergens.test.mjs exist; tests run with `node --test` (memory applied without being restated), no package.json dependencies, no npm install; the output shows all passing with a count. The chorizo toastie is reported as having an ingredient still being checked, and its known allergens (cereals containing gluten, milk, fish) are still listed.

turns.say: Commit that.
turns.expect: A second commit containing lib/ and test/; `git status` clean afterwards (site/ ignored).

turns.say: Let's clear the rest of notes/open-questions.md. I'm heading into the kitchen, so ask me every remaining question on it now, all at once, one separate question for each, and I'll answer them from my phone. Leave the may-contain one for later, I want to think about that.
turns.expect: NEEDS-YOU cards #2 and #3 OPEN AT ONCE: at least two ask_user cards raised in the same turn and both visible in the tray before either is answered: the scone price (town vs Douglas) and the soda bread oat milk vs buttermilk; the mince pie price is a likely third. No card about may-contain in this turn. No data edited before the answers arrive. needsyou.tsv shows each answered from guidance, and answering one does not close its sibling (siblingsOpen stays correct).

turns.say: Apply my answers to the data, rerun the tests, and show me the rows for the scone, the soda bread and the mince pie now.
turns.expect: data/dishes.csv: scone one price 3.50 for both shops; mince pie 2.50 each with the four-for-9.00 offer recorded; house-recipes soda bread uses oat milk (buttermilk gone). The soda bread slice still lists milk (butter on the side) and cereals containing gluten (wheat, oats). notes/open-questions.md updated so only may-contain (and the chorizo check) remain open. Tests re-run, all passing.

turns.say: Now the site itself. I want it to look like it belongs to this bakery, not like a template. Before any code, give me a design plan: the colours, the type, a rough layout sketch and what makes it theirs. Remember it runs on the counter iPad with no wifi, so nothing can be loaded from the internet.
turns.expect: The frontend-design skill loads (visible skill load) and its process shows: a plan with 4-6 named hex colours, typefaces with roles (system fonts or a local font file, no Google Fonts or CDN URL), an ASCII layout sketch, and a review of the plan against the brief. No site files written yet. Loading stack-angular/stack-fastapi or an Atlassian skill is a precision miss.

turns.say: Good, build it. node build.mjs should generate site/index.html (the menu by section, each dish with its price and its allergens), site/allergens.html (the full matrix: dishes down, the 14 allergens across) and site/style.css, all from the data files. Put a filter at the top of the menu, 'I can't have…', with a checkbox per allergen that hides any dish containing a ticked one. Add tests for the build output.
turns.expect: build.mjs, site/index.html, site/allergens.html, site/style.css exist; `grep -rn 'http' site/` finds no external stylesheet, font or script URL; every price renders as €x.xx (e.g. €3.50, €9.90, €10.50); allergens appear as words (memory); the matrix has 14 allergen columns and one row per dish; the filter is vanilla JS; new build tests pass under node --test.

turns.say: Now the may-contain question from my notes. Sort it out on the site.
turns.expect: NEEDS-YOU card #4: an ask_user card about the may-contain policy (Siobhán wants it on everything, the person is unsure) — a decision only the owner can make, so goose must not pick a policy itself. turns.expect: Granola bowl text shows its allergens (cereals containing gluten, nuts, sulphites, milk) plus the may-contain line; the scone shows cereals containing gluten, eggs, milk and no may-contain line; the footer kitchen line is on index.html and allergens.html; prices €6.50 and €3.50.
